## Identification of Data Sources

<!-- Describe what data is available and where it comes from. -->

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-sources
#| echo: false
#| output: true

# Read the data into a data.table 
dtDS <-  fread(text = "
  Data Source         , Time-Span, Granularity, Origin, Content
  article master data , > 2020   ,            , SAP S4, article hierachy
  customer master data, > 2020   ,            , SAP S4, customer hierachy
  historical sales    , > 2020   , daily      , SAP S4, customer orders + free-of-charge 
  historical forecasts, > 2023   , monhtly    , QAD   , monthly pre- & post Demand review forecasts
")

# Create a styled kableExtra table
dtDS |> 
  kbl(
    caption   = "Data Sources ",
    col.names = names(dtDS),
    align     = c("l", "l", "l"),
    booktabs  = TRUE
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position   = "left",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )
```

## Initial Data Collection Report

<!-- Summarize how data was obtained and any issues during acquisition: -->

All data is Sourced from *BioBalance* SAP-BI system using the SAP Open Hub Technology.

![Data Collection pipelines](/images/dp01.png){#dp01 fig-align="center"}

The data is extracted from the underlying tables, joined, filtered and transformed and written to a CSV file.

<!-- Data filters applied (Doctype's, Item category, ...) -->

<!-- exclude units pak and DS   -->

BUOM <!-- exclude Promotion articles --> PRAT7 <!-- only master data which is relevant for the analysis -->

<!-- DuckDB tranformations -->

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-collection
#| echo: false
#| output: true

# Read the data into a data.table 
dtDC <-  fread(text = "
  Data Source         , Type, Extract Date, Records, GB  , Key
  article master data , MD  ,             ,        ,     , Article     
  customer master data, MD  ,             ,        ,     , Customer
  historical sales    , TD  ,             ,        ,     , Date; Article; Plant; Customer
  historical forecasts, TD  ,             ,        ,     , Date; Article; Plant; CustHier3
")

# Create a styled kableExtra table
dtDC |> 
  kbl(
    caption   = "Data Collection ",
    col.names = names(dtDC),
    align     = c("l", "l", "l"),
    booktabs  = TRUE
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position   = "left",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-description-hierarchy
#| echo: false
#| include: false

OD <- "C:\\Users\\flori\\OneDrive\\ET\\pythia\\data"

# Read the data into a data.table
dtMAT <- wb_read(
  file      = file.path(OD, "ET2BB.xlsx"),
  sheet     = "MASP",
  start_row = 19,
  start_col = 6,
  skip_empty_cols = TRUE,
  skip_empty_rows = TRUE
) %T>%
  setDT() %T>%
  setnames(
    c(4, 6, 8), 
    c("ProdCat", "SubCat", "Family")
  ) %>%
  .[, .(ProdCat, SubCat, Family, Material)] %>%
  unique()

dtCUST <- wb_read(
  file      = file.path(OD, "ET2BB.xlsx"),
  sheet     = "CUST",
  start_row = 19,
  start_col = 9,
  skip_empty_cols = TRUE,
  skip_empty_rows = TRUE
) %T>%
  setDT() %T>%
  setnames(c(1), c("KEY")  ) 

dtCUST_H1 <- wb_read(
  file      = file.path(OD, "ET2BB.xlsx"),
  sheet     = "CUST_H1",
  start_row = 1,
  start_col = 1,
  skip_empty_cols = TRUE,
  skip_empty_rows = TRUE
) %T>%
  setDT() %T>%
  setnames(c(1), c("KEY")  )

dtCST <- 
  dtCUST_H1[dtCUST, on = .(KEY), nomatch = 0] %T>%
  setnames(
    c(4, 7, 9, 11),
    c("Channel", "Key_Account", "Account", "SoldTo")
  ) %>%
  .[, .(Channel, Key_Account, Account, SoldTo, Customer)] %>%
  unique()
```



::: {#article_hier .figure}
::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-description-hierarchy-plot
#| echo: false
#| output: true

collapsibleTree(
  dtMAT,
  hierarchy   = c("ProdCat", "SubCat", "Family"),
  root        = "Articles",
  width       = "100%",
  zoomable    = TRUE,
  fillByLevel = TRUE,
  fill        = "#38e56d"
)
```
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}
```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-description-hierarchy-article-treemap
#| echo: false
#| output: true

library(treemapify)

# Count of Family items per Category&Sub Category combo
treemap_dt <- 
  dtMAT[, .(ProdCat, SubCat, Family)]      %>%
  unique()                                 %>%
  .[, count:= .N, by = .(ProdCat, SubCat)]

# Use only level1-level2 for compactness
ggplot(treemap_dt, aes(area = count, fill = ProdCat, label = SubCat)) +
  geom_treemap() +
  geom_treemap_text(colour = "white", place = "centre", grow = TRUE) 

```
:::

Interactive Article Hierarchy, click on the nodes to expand/collapse
:::

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-description-hierarchy-article
#| echo: false
#| output: true

dtMAT_tab <- dtMAT[, .(
  SubCat_Count   = uniqueN(SubCat),
  Family_Count   = uniqueN(Family),
  Material_Count = uniqueN(Material)
), by = ProdCat][order(ProdCat)]

# Create a styled kableExtra table
dtMAT_tab |> 
  kbl(
    caption   = "Summary: Article Hierachy",
    col.names = names(dtMAT),
    align     = rep("l", ncol(dtMAT_tab)),
    booktabs  = TRUE
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position   = "left",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )

dtCST_tab <- dtCST[, .(
  KAM_count      = uniqueN(Key_Account),
  ACC_Count      = uniqueN(Account),
  SoldTo_Count   = uniqueN(SoldTo),
  Customer_Count = uniqueN(Customer)
), by = Channel][order(Channel)]

dtCST_tab |>
  kbl(
    caption   = "Summary: Customer Hierachy",
    col.names = names(dtCST),
    align     = rep("l", ncol(dtCST)),
    booktabs  = TRUE
  ) |> 
  kable_styling(
    full_width = FALSE,
    position   = "left",
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )


```
